title: Longest Bitwise-Disjoint Subarray
description: You are given an array `nums` consisting of positive integers. A contiguous subarray of `nums` is called bitwise-disjoint if the bitwise AND of every pair of elements at different indices within the subarray equals `0`. Return the length of the longest bitwise-disjoint subarray (every single-element subarray is trivially bitwise-disjoint).
hints: In a bitwise-disjoint subarray, no two elements may share a `1` at the same bit position, so the bitwise OR of the window captures every currently occupied bit.
Use a sliding window with a bitmask `used`: while `used & nums[right] != 0`, remove `nums[left]` via `used ^= nums[left]` and advance `left`.

examples.explanation: The subarray [3, 8, 48] has 3&8=0, 3&48=0, and 8&48=0, giving length 3.
Every adjacent pair shares at least one set bit, so the longest valid subarray has length 1.
All five powers of two are pairwise disjoint, giving length 5.
